answer_core:
Do not confront the partner, investigate on your own, access systems unusually, make legal conclusions, or pick a reporting channel yourself. Tonight, write a precise private account of what you saw, preserve your own notes, tell your spouse only in broad strokes, and contact two or three independent whistleblower attorneys.

Your first move is counsel selection, not reporting. Ask each attorney how they decide between internal reporting to GC, reporting to an audit committee or independent board channel, and external filing. Also ask for examples of situations where they advised internal-first or audit-committee-first rather than filing first, so you can test whether their incentives are pulling too hard toward a filing path.

Attend Wednesday normally unless counsel gives you a different script first. If the partner raises the encounter, keep your response narrow: do not deny, elaborate, confront, investigate, or be alone with the partner if avoidable. Do not volunteer theories or conclusions. Keep your behavior ordinary and reversible.

This is high risk, so do not let fear push you into filing before counsel reviews the facts, but do not let fear make you do nothing either. Get independent counsel involved quickly, preserve what you personally know, and let counsel choose the safest reporting route.
